_note: Illustration slots: one per chapter where a picture earns its place. 'scene' is the brief for an artist or an image model; 'pd' lists public-domain works known to depict the scene (to be verified against the source museum/library record before use).

3.scene: Troy as the medieval North imagined it: a walled city of twelve kingdoms; the boy Trór (Thor) lifting ten bearskins at twelve winters.
pd: Medieval manuscript views of Troy (e.g. Bibliothèque nationale de France, Roman de Troie illuminations)

4.scene: Odin and his household leaving Turkey for the north with a great following, entering Saxland, Reidgothland and the Danish lands.
pd: Lorenz Frølich, illustrations to the Edda (1890s)

5.scene: Odin founding Sigtún by the lake and setting up twelve chieftains as judges, in the manner of Troy.

1.scene: Gefjun ploughing Zealand out of Sweden with four giant oxen (her sons); the land dragged west into the sea, the lake Lögrinn left behind.

2.scene: Gylfi as Gangleri entering the hall roofed with golden shields; a juggler with seven knives in the air; three high-seats one above another with Hár, Jafnhár and Þriði.
pd: Icelandic manuscript NKS 1867 4to (Ólafur Brynjúlfsson, 1760), the three kings

5.scene: Ymir asleep in Ginnungagap, sweating out the first frost-giants; a man and a woman growing from under his left arm.

6.scene: The cow Auðumbla licking the salty rime-stones; Búri emerging as the stones are licked away, while Ymir feeds on her milk.
pd: Nicolai Abildgaard, 'Ymir suckling the cow Audhumla' (1790)

8.scene: The sons of Borr carrying Ymir into the middle of the void: the world made of his body, the sky of his skull held up by four dwarfs.
pd: Lorenz Frølich, the sons of Borr lifting Ymir

9.scene: Three gods by the sea-shore finding two logs, Askr and Embla, and giving them breath, wit and warmth.

11.scene: Sól and Máni driving the sun and moon across the sky in their chariots, two wolves running behind them.
pd: John Charles Dollman, 'The Wolves Pursuing Sol and Mani' (1909)

13.scene: Bifröst, the burning three-coloured bridge from earth to heaven.

15.scene: The ash Yggdrasil with its three roots: the Norns Urðr, Verðandi and Skuld at the well, the eagle in the crown, Níðhöggr gnawing below.

20.scene: Odin enthroned with the ravens Huginn and Muninn and the wolves Geri and Freki.
pd: NKS 1867 4to (1760), Odin with ravens and wolves

21.scene: Thor in his goat-drawn chariot with Mjöllnir, the belt of strength and the iron gloves.
pd: Mårten Eskil Winge, 'Thor's Fight with the Giants' (1872)

23.scene: Skaði choosing a husband by his feet; Njörðr and Skaði unable to agree where to live, mountains against sea-shore.
pd: H. L. M., 'Skadi Hunting in the Mountains' (1901)

27.scene: Heimdallr at the end of heaven with the horn Gjallarhorn, by the bridge.

34.scene: The binding of Fenrir with Gleipnir; Týr placing his hand in the wolf's mouth as a pledge; Jörmungandr cast into the sea; Hel sent to Niflheim.
pd: Lorenz Frølich, the binding of Fenrir

37.scene: Freyr on Hliðskjálf seeing Gerðr in Gymir's garth; Skírnir riding to woo her with the sword given away.

38.scene: Valhöll: the einherjar feasting on the boar Sæhrímnir, Odin giving his meat to the wolves, the ravens on his shoulders.

42.scene: The giant master-builder and his stallion Svaðilfari hauling stones for the wall of Ásgarðr; Loki as a mare luring the horse away; the birth of Sleipnir.

45.scene: Thor, Loki, Þjálfi and Röskva sleeping in Skrýmir's glove; Thor striking the sleeping giant with Mjöllnir.
pd: Louis Huard, 'The Giant Skrymir and Thor' (1891)

46.scene: In Útgarða-Loki's hall: Loki's eating contest with Logi, Þjálfi racing Hugi, Thor drinking from the horn, lifting the cat, wrestling the old woman Elli.

48.scene: Thor fishing with Hymir, the ox-head bait, the Midgard Serpent on the hook, Hymir cutting the line.
pd: Henry Fuseli, 'Thor battering the Midgard Serpent' (1790)

49.scene: The death of Baldr: the gods shooting at him, blind Höðr guided by Loki, the mistletoe shot; Hermóðr riding Sleipnir down to Hel; Baldr's funeral ship Hringhorni pushed out by Hyrrokkin.
pd: W. G. Collingwood, 'The Funeral of Baldr' (1908)

50.scene: Loki bound over three stones with his son's entrails, the serpent above him, Sigyn holding the bowl.
pd: Gosforth Cross, the bound figure (10th c.)

51.scene: Ragnarök: the Fenris-wolf with jaws from earth to heaven, the serpent spewing venom, Surtr with the flaming sword, Odin against the wolf, Thor against the serpent, Víðarr tearing the wolf's jaws.

53.scene: After the fire: the earth rising green from the sea, Víðarr and Váli, Móði and Magni with Mjöllnir, Líf and Lífþrasir in Hoddmímir's holt.
pd: Emil Doepler, 'Nach dem Untergang' / Líf and Lífþrasir (1905)

54.scene: Gangleri standing alone on an open plain, the hall and city vanished.

2.scene: Þjazi as an eagle carrying Loki off by the pole stuck to the eagle's back; Iðunn with her apples lured into the wood.

3.scene: Loki in Freyja's falcon-shape flying back with Iðunn turned into a nut, Þjazi the eagle pursuing and burned at the wall of Ásgarðr.

5.scene: Kvasir made from the spittle of the gods; the dwarfs Fjalar and Galar brewing the mead of poetry in Óðrerir, Són and Boðn.
pd: Franz Stassen, 'Odin and the mead' (1920s – check date)

6.scene: Odin as Bölverkr boring through the mountain with the auger Rati, Gunnlöð and the three draughts, Odin flying off as an eagle with Suttungr behind.

24.scene: Thor's duel with Hrungnir on the frontier: the giant with his whetstone and stone shield, Mökkurkálfi the clay giant, Þjálfi; the whetstone lodged in Thor's head.

26.scene: Thor wading the river Vimur with Gríðr's staff against Geirröðr's daughters; Geirröðr throwing the glowing iron, Thor catching it with the iron gloves.

43.scene: The sons of Ívaldi and the dwarf Sindri forging Sif's golden hair, Skíðblaðnir, Gungnir, Draupnir, Gullinbursti and Mjöllnir; Loki as a fly biting Brokkr.
pd: Elmer Boyd Smith, 'The third gift — an enormous hammer' (1902)

46.scene: Otter's ransom: Loki killing Otr, the gods covering the skin with Andvari's gold; Andvari as a pike; the cursed ring Andvaranaut.
pd: Arthur Rackham, 'The Rhinegold and the Valkyrie' illustrations (1910)

47.scene: Sigurðr slaying Fáfnir from the pit, roasting the heart, understanding the birds; Reginn's death.
pd: Hylestad stave church portal carvings (12th c.)

52.scene: Fenja and Menja grinding at the mill Grótti for King Fróði; Mýsingr's ship sinking with the mill, the sea turned salt.

54.scene: Hrólfr kraki sowing gold on the Fýrisvellir to delay King Aðils's pursuing riders.

62.scene: The Hjaðningavíg: Hildr waking the fallen every night so that the battle of Högni and Heðinn goes on until Ragnarök.
pd: Stora Hammars I picture stone, Gotland (8th c.)

1.scene: King Hákon Hákonarson and Earl Skúli Bárðarson, the dedicatees of Háttatal, in a hall at Bergen c. 1220.
pd: Flateyjarbók (GKS 1005 fol.) illuminations of Norwegian kings
